newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes fall late, Feb grades wind down.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes fall late, Feb grades wind down.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices fell late Thursday in a continuing trend tied to lower heating oil prices, traders said.
Most traders were trying to wind up February positions in the wake of the Feb NYMEX expiry on Tuesday. February barrels are still abundant, however, pushing February into contango with March.
March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was trading at $24.15-25 a barrel, down 10 cents from late Wednesday.
The Feb/March WTI roll was last done at minus 25 cents, putting Feb WTI around $23.90-24.00 a barrel, traders said.
The depressed roll continued to drive grade activity.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was talked at WTI/Cushing plus 20-30 cents.
WTI/Midland was heard done at WTI/Cushing minus 35-40 cents a barrel, up about 10 cents from Wednesday.
West Texas Sour/Midland was last done at minus $1.55 a barrel.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus was done at $1.55 a barrel.
In the aftermarket, WTI/Cushing was talked at $24.16-20 a barrel, traders said.
